subject: Re: Performance guardrails & POC owner map
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Bennett <abennett@dwell.ai>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@dwell.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: POC scope & initial guardrails

Thanks again for the time this morning — helpful to understand the 3 main goals you have for the POC (summarized below). I wanted to capture concrete next steps, proposed success criteria, and owners so we can kick off next week if this looks good.

High-level objectives you shared:
- Real-time inference for conversational assistant (internal product team)
- Latency must be low enough to keep UI interactions under 250ms perceived delay
- Control cost to within prototype budget (~$1k-$1.5k/month equivalent)

Proposed POC scope (3-week technical evaluation):
1) Baseline run: 1 model variant, 2 workload patterns (short chat, long-context retrieval)
2) Instrumentation: token-level latency, p50/p95, throughput (tokens/sec), cost per 1k tokens
3) Quality checks: response correctness on 120 prompt set + hallucination inspection on 20 edge cases

Initial success criteria (draft):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation <= 200ms on short-chat median turn (network excluded)
- Throughput: sustain 120 concurrent short-chat sessions with <= 250ms p95
- Cost: average cost/token <= $0.0006 (target for prototype budget)
- Quality: >= 88% pass rate on the 120 prompt set (scored by your SMEs), hallucination rate < 3% on edge set

Owners (proposed):
- Redwood technical owner: Marcus Lin (Solutions Engineering) — model config, smoke tests, instrumentation
- Redwood engagement lead: Irene Choi — timeline, deliverables, status reporting
- Customer owner: Alex Bennett (Data Platform) — dataset access, scoring, run coordination

Next steps (action items to confirm in reply):
- Alex: confirm dataset access and an initial sample (50 prompts) by Mon Feb 22
- Procurement: confirm any needed NDAs or MSA addenda (cc'd procurement if needed)
- Redwood: send POC template + instrumentation checklist (see attachment)
- Schedule: propose Wed Feb 23 for a 30-min kickoff to align roles and access

Attachments: RI_POC_Template_v2.xlsx (POC milestones + measurement templates), sample_latency_baseline.csv (example instrumentation CSV)

If the above looks accurate, reply-all with any edits and we’ll lock the kickoff.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi

Thanks, Irene — that summary is spot on. A few notes from our side:
- We can share the 50-sample seed set by EOD Mon (Feb 22). I’ll include labels where available.
- Procurement: we typically need a short SOW + data access addendum. I’ve looped in procurement to help.
- One ask on metrics: can we capture token-level cost and per-request cold-start timing separately? For our infra team that split helps a lot.

Also, slight tweak on latency targets: the product PM suggested p95 UI budget is 250ms including network, so if you can provide an infra-only p95 target (your side) to mix with our network numbers that’d be ideal.

Agree on Wed Feb 23 kickoff — 11:00am PT works for me.

Appreciate it — Alex

Subject: Re: Follow-up: POC scope & initial guardrails

Thanks Alex — great clarifications. I updated the targets below to split network vs infra so we have a clear measurement plan. Also included a proposed evaluation rubric and timeline. Please review and flag any changes before the kickoff Wed.

Revised success criteria (measured as noted):
- Latency (infra-only): p95 model generation time <= 200ms. You will record client-side RTT/network; we will provide model-only timings.
- Latency (end-to-end for acceptance): p95 <= 250ms using your seat-of-network sample set. Acceptance will use your network numbers + our model-only numbers added in the runbook.
- Throughput: sustain 120 concurrent short-chat sessions with aggregate throughput >= 8k tokens/sec and p95 per-turn <= 250ms (infra-only).
- Cost: target average cost/token <= $0.0006 across evaluated model variant; provide breakdown tokenized vs overhead.
- Quality: pass rate >= 88% on 120 prompt review (binary pass/fail by your SMEs) and hallucination incidents < 3% on the 20-case edge set. We will run automated NER-based hallucination checks and hand-annotate failures.

Evaluation plan highlights:
- Dataset: Alex to provide sample seed (50) by Feb 22; full 120 prompt set by Feb 25. We’ll agree on the SME scoring rubric in kickoff.
- Instrumentation: Redwood will add token-level tracing and per-request timing hooks; we’ll publish a CSV with p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost columns.
- Regression checks: nightly smoke run during week 2; final acceptance run at the end of week 3 (report + raw logs).

Timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (prep): access + sample set (Feb 22–23)
- Week 1: baseline runs + configs (Feb 24–Mar 2)
- Week 2: stress/throughput tests + quality scoring (Mar 3–Mar 9)
- Week 3: acceptance run + final report (Mar 10–Mar 16)

Owners & contacts:
- Redwood technical: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai> — model config, instrumentation, run manager
- Redwood engagement: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai> — schedule, reporting
- Customer technical: Alex Bennett <abennett@dwell.ai> — dataset, SME scoring
- Customer procurement: Procurement <procurement@dwell.ai> — contracts/SOW

Action items (please reply with confirmations):
- Alex: confirm you’ll provide 50-sample seed by EOD Mon Feb 22 (confirmed in your reply)
- Procurement: indicate whether a short SOW is sufficient or you need a redline to the MSA
- Marcus: I attached the POC template + example CSV — Marcus, can you confirm instrumentation hooks are included in this template?

Attachments: RI_POC_Template_v2.xlsx, sample_latency_baseline.csv

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Irene
